anchored_definition_en: surrounding linguistic or situational settings in which something appears or is used
reviewer_1_definition_en: the surrounding linguistic or situational settings in which something appears, is interpreted, or is used
reviewer_2_definition_en: the surrounding circumstances, settings, or linguistic material in which something occurs or is interpreted
reviewer_3_definition_en: Either the linguistic surroundings of a word or token, or the broader setting or circumstances in which a method or result applies.

anchored_definition_en: layers in which each output unit is connected to all input units from the previous layer
reviewer_1_definition_en: neural network layers, typically implemented as linear layers, in which each output unit connects to all inputs from the preceding layer
reviewer_2_definition_en: neural-network layers in which every output unit is connected to all inputs from the preceding layer, commonly implemented as Linear layers
reviewer_3_definition_en: Linear neural-network layers that can be stacked to form a multilayer perceptron.

anchored_definition_en: done directly on the existing object, memory, or arrangement rather than creating a separate replacement; by extension, already established or set up.
reviewer_1_definition_en: either directly modifying an existing object or memory rather than replacing it, or already present and established in the required arrangement
reviewer_2_definition_en: either modifying an existing object or memory directly rather than replacing it, or already established, arranged, or ready
reviewer_3_definition_en: Either by modifying the same stored object rather than replacing it, or already present, installed, or ready.
